Newbie Linux Install Challenges: I need help partitioning hard drive space

Basically you need a partition table on the drive and then you're able to create partitions, which each have a file system. To be able to use the file system it needs to be mounted, then it is accessible at its mountpoint directory. For a simple install the root partition which is mounted at / is enough and 100GB should be big enough.

Some file systems can't be increased in size and many can't be decreased.

Both recent experience and some studies that made it to front page reflect a solution to this.

Your natural inclination is to present a case of opposing new information and facts of education to back it up. Ask anyone including yourself if you have any beliefs that you know to be wrong. Every belief everyone has feels right. Everyone has some level of discomfort they feel when they discover a belief they have is wrong, and a lifelong pavlov style training in the brain of getting discomfort every time opposing information is presented makes their brains shut down and get defensive when opposing information is presented. The studies show intelligence decreases, emotions increase. The studies also show that people like this, and its most people, actually get more resolute in their beliefs when they are challenged.

As much as you have this massive emotion pushing you to explain reason to them, it will probably only make the problem worse. The actual solution to people not open to conflicting information and education, is not to make them feel threatened about their belief...its a bit of inception.

Anyone that has an unfounded belief, has just that, no foundation. Instead of presenting facts and reason, simply have them present theirs. Continue to question them about why they believe what they do. The less they know about your beliefs or views the better. If they know where you are heading with your line of questioning they will likely be intelligent enough to start resisting. Just keep asking questions until you get to the bottom of it. The questions will get more and more basic and stupid sounding as you get further in. This is a sign you are getting close. Once they hit a dead end they will realize themselves their own reasoning. If it is faulty on a basic level or conflicts with their other beliefs it will fall apart at this point.

This wont always work...some people are ok with what they discover. For example discussed with family explaining that government licensing and control of relationships through marriage laws was started as a way of punishing interracial relationships. It is now being used to punish same genital relationships. At first they cited things they had heard about benefits downsides etc. After 10 minutes of asking why over and over, they finally admitted/realized it was because it is gross. Their words. And further confirmed that being gross is the only reason. And then they said that something bothering or grossing a bunch of people out is enough reason to outlaw or punish said behaviour. Like someone being naked in public. It bothers most people so it should be stopped according to them, even though it hurts no one in a serious way. That licensing and punishing of relationships is acceptable for this reason. But hey, even worse case, you know the foundations of their belief and likely avoided a emotional conflict that just made their beliefs stronger.

The thing that a whole lot of people don't understand is that when it comes to people, its really not about what you say it, but the kind of person who is behind the words.

Simply disagreeing with them and stating facts assumes that they are receptive to logical arguments. If they were receptive to logical arguments, they would not be racist in the first place.

If you want people to change their behavior, you have to appeal to the emotional side. You have to identify specifically what makes them happy in regards to you, and then "condition" them to associate a negative outcome in regards to this when they say racist things.
